text:
Maya K: Heads-up — we got a customer PM about p99 latency spikes hitting their API calls in eu-west today. They say it started ~08:12 UTC and correlates with a burst of 5xxs and >1.2s TLS handshakes. attaching their curl timings and a traceroute they ran: 

Maya K: curl -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}
' -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -> 0.230 0.980 1.205
Maya K: traceroute to api.redwood.example (34.120.23.55), 30 hops max
Maya K:  1  10.0.0.2  0.5 ms
Maya K:  5  52.17.9.1  12.0 ms
Maya K: 10  34.120.23.55  320.4 ms

eng-oncall-bot: Alert: customer-eu-p99-latency spike detected (slo_eu_api.p99) at 2024-10-04T08:15:00Z — incidents/INC-9241 created.

Samir: looking. can you drop the observability dashboard link and request id from the customer? also which customer/org?

Maya K: Org: Acme Retail. customer provided request-id: req_0a7c3ef. Dashboard: https://obs.redwood.internal/d/aw5eu/api-p99?var-org=acme&from=now-2h&to=now

Olivia: I can see a spike in p95->p99 at 08:11-08:18 for eu-west1 egress. Intermittent RTT jump to ~300ms for a subset of backend hosts. No code deploy at that time from infra change log.

Chris R: can we confirm if this is DNS/route or TLS handshake churn? grab TLS logs from ingress for req_0a7c3ef and check for new connections vs session resumes. Also tcpdump on the affected pop might show path changes.

Maya K: attaching excerpts from ingress logs: 
Maya K: [ingress-euw1] req=req_0a7c3ef tls_handshake_time=0.848 session_resume=false upstream_ip=34.120.23.55 route_asn=12345
Maya K: [ingress-euw1] req=req_xxx tls_handshake_time=0.045 session_resume=true upstream_ip=34.120.23.55 route_asn=12346

Samir: interesting — same upstream ip but different route_asn for slow vs fast. smells like BGP path oscillation / temporary path inflation. Could be GSLB steering changes too.

Olivia: I checked control-plane logs: there was a routing policy tweak at 08:10 to prefer a new peer for a small prefix (rollout 10%). It looks like a fraction of customers got flapped between peers. That could trigger longer AS paths and extra RTTs.

Chris R: mitigation ideas: 
- roll back the routing policy change (quick) to restore stable AS paths 
- enable route pinning for critical API prefixes to avoid multi-peer flip-flop 
- for affected customers, enable TLS session ticket reuse hints and lower handshake retries temporarily
- set a short automation to shift traffic away from the affected fabric to eu-west2 as fallback for the rollout window

Samir: +1 rollback first. Olivia, can you run the rollback? If it’s a config flag, we can revert target to previous operator. Add a canary key to avoid global flip.

Olivia: rolling back now (reverting peer-preference for prefix 34.120.0.0/16). will post update in 60s.

eng-oncall-bot: ChangeEvent: route-policy-revert by Olivia @ 08:20 UTC — config change id cfg_8892 queued.

Maya K: customer says tail latency dropped after 08:22, from 1.2s -> 0.18s median and p99 back to ~220ms. They requested a timeline and root cause.

Chris R: capture for postmortem: 
- root cause: partial rollout of new peer preference caused multi-path AS path oscillation and path inflation for subset of egress flows, increasing RTT and TLS handshake times 
- immediate mitigation: rollback routing-policy, enable route pinning for API prefixes, temporary eu-west2 fallback for affected tenant, request customer-side caching of TLS sessions where possible

Samir: I'll file INC-9241 update to customer with timeline, attach traceroute/tls logs, and mark as resolved pending postmortem. Assign postmortem to Olivia + NetInfra.

Maya K: thanks — customer replied :thumbsup: and will re-open if it reappears.

Chris R: follow-ups for postmortem: measure how many prefixes rollouts used >5% audience and create a rollout safety check to ensure BGP path stability (maybe simulate AS path delta). Also consider EDNS client subnet interactions with GSLB.

Olivia: noted. creating a runbook entry for route-rollouts and adding an automated pre-rollout traceroute sample for target prefixes.

Samir: good. closing thread unless anyone sees residual errors.

Maya K: closing — will ping when postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
